[[United States men's national basketball team|Team]]}} | years8 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team8 = [[New York Knicks]] }} '''Andre Jamal Drummond''' (born August 10, 1993) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[New York Knicks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). A [[Center (basketball)|center]], he was selected by the [[Detroit Pistons]] in the first round of the [[2012 NBA draft]] with the ninth overall pick. Drummond was one of the top-rated basketball players in the high school class of 2011 and played one season of [[college basketball]] with the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut Huskies]] before declaring for the draft. He was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] with Detroit in 2013, and was named an All-Star for the first time in 2016. He was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in 2020. After reaching a buyout agreement with Cleveland in 2021, he joined the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for the remainder of the 2020–21 season. Drummond has also played for the [[Brooklyn Nets]], [[Philadelphia 76ers]] and [[Chicago Bulls]]. Drummond has perennially been among the league leaders in rebounding. He was a member of the [[2014 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team|2014 U.S. national team]] that won a gold medal in the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup]]. ==Early life== [[File:Austin Colbert Andre Drummond (5444482028).jpg|thumb|left|Drummond (right) as a high school player in 2010]] Born in [[Mount Vernon, New York]], in 1993 to Jamaican parents,{{cite web |title=The Canadians are coming to the NBA: No, the Caribbean is coming |url=http://www.caribbean-events.com/article/canadians-are-coming-nba-no-caribbean-coming |website=caribbean-events.com |access-date=January 7, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140605053321/http://www.caribbean-events.com/article/canadians-are-coming-nba-no-caribbean-coming |archive-date=June 5, 2014 |date=February 15, 2014}} Drummond moved to [[Middletown, Connecticut]], as a 7-year-old with his mother and sister, then went to Woodrow Wilson Middle School before starting high school at Capital Preparatory Magnet School in [[Hartford, Connecticut|Hartford]].{{cite web |last=Pelletier |first=Joe |title=Before NBA Draft, Andre Drummond finds comfort in home court |url=https://www.middletownpress.com/news/article/Before-NBA-Draft-Andre-Drummond-finds-comfort-in-11832327.php |work=The Middletown Press |access-date=January 7, 2020 |date=June 26, 2012}} During his [[freshman]] year, he averaged 12.7 points, 11.9 rebounds and 6.5 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athletes/cIiwRqjEhkK-vwwyncOong/basketball-winter-07-08/stats-andre-drummond.htm |title=Andre Drummond's (Hartford, CT) High School Basketball Stats |publisher=Maxpreps.com |access-date=October 27, 2013}} He improved during his [[sophomore]] year at Capital Prep, averaging 20.2 points, 16.6 rebounds, 7.2 blocks and 4.5 steals per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athletes/6HpV6s2d7Emo9pJuUCdhuw/basketball-winter-08-09/stats-andre-drummond.htm |title=Andre Drummond's (Hartford, CT) High School Basketball Stats |publisher=Maxpreps.com |access-date=October 27, 2013}} After two years at Capital Preparatory Magnet School, he transferred to [[St. Thomas More School (Connecticut)|St. Thomas More]] in [[Oakdale, Connecticut|Oakdale]], where he [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] and repeated his sophomore year as he recovered from a stress fracture in his foot.{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Abrams|title=Giant Steps|date=October 16, 2013|work=Grantland|url=https://grantland.com/features/the-life-career-detroit-pistons-center-andre-drummond/|access-date=March 11, 2023}}{{cite web|first=Katy|last=Daigle|title=Drummond No. 1 Sophomore|date=September 4, 2009|work=Hartford Courant|url=https://www.courant.com/2009/09/04/drummond-no-1-sophomore/|access-date=March 11, 2023}} At St. Thomas More, Drummond was one of the most dominating [[Center (basketball)|centers]] in high school basketball.{{cite news|last1=Biancardi |first1=Paul |author-link1=Paul Biancardi |last2=Finkelstein |first2=Adam |name-list-style=and |title=Andre Drummond to UConn surprises |date=August 26, 2011 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/6900273 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107130930/http://espn.go.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/6900273/still-questions-regarding-andre-drummond-commitment-connecticut |archive-date=November 7, 2012 |url-status=live}} He spent two years at St. Thomas More and led the team to the national prep championship in 2011, alongside future NBA player [[Damion Lee]]. He graduated in the spring that year. Drummond was rated as the No. 1 player in the class of 2011 by [[ESPN]] and NBADraft.net, while being ranked No. 2 player by [[Rivals.com]] and [[Scout.com]].{{cite news|last=Demling |first=Jody |title=Kentucky recruiting board – Class of 2012 |date=July 5, 2011 |newspaper=[[The Courier-Journal]] |url=http://blogs.courier-journal.com/jodydemling/2011/07/05/kentucky-recruiting-board-class-of-2012/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120707144709/http://blogs.courier-journal.com/jodydemling/2011/07/05/kentucky-recruiting-board-class-of-2012/ |archive-date=July 7, 2012 |url-status=live}}{{cite web |url=http://www.nbadraft.net/2012mock_draft |title=2012 Mock Draft |work=NBADraft.net |publisher=Sports Phenoms, Inc |date=August 15, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110829230613/http://www.nbadraft.net/2012mock_draft |archive-date=August 29, 2011 |url-status=dead |access-date=July 20, 2011 }} In the summer of 2010, Drummond was a member of the gold medal-winning [[United States men's national basketball team|United States team]] at the [[2010 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]]. He helped lead team USA to a 111–80 victory over [[Poland national basketball team|Poland]] in the gold medal game.{{cite web|url=http://basketball.teamusa.org/news/2010/07/11/usa-men-s-u17-team-runs-away-with-gold-destroys-poland-111-80/37198 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100715110802/http://basketball.teamusa.org/news/2010/07/11/usa-men-s-u17-team-runs-away-with-gold-destroys-poland-111-80/37198 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 15, 2010 |title=USA Men's U17 Team Runs Away With Gold, Destroys Poland 111–80 |publisher=Basketball.TeamUSA.org |date=July 11, 2010 |access-date=January 21, 2011}} ==College career== Drummond initially declared he would spend a [[postgraduate year]] at [[Wilbraham & Monson Academy]] in 2011–12.{{cite news |last=Chardis |first=Phil |title=UConn basketball: Drummond opts for post-graduate year |date=August 11, 2011 |newspaper=[[Journal Inquirer]] |url=http://www.journalinquirer.com/articles/2011/08/11/sports/doc4e43e6a4f0cd3656861423.txt |quote=Andre Drummond, the 6-foot-11 center from Middletown who is considered to be one of the top scholastic basketball players in the country and a prime recruiting target for the University of Connecticut, announced Wednesday that he will spend a post-graduate year at Wilbraham & Monson Academy (Wilbraham, Mass.) in 2011–12.}}{{cite web|url=http://www.collegiatehoops.net/2010/08/despite-class-andre-drummond-will-still.html |title=Despite The Class, Andre Drummond Will Still Be The Best Center |publisher=CollegiateHoops.net |access-date=January 21, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110203010116/http://www.collegiatehoops.net/2010/08/despite-class-andre-drummond-will-still.html |archive-date=February 3, 2011}} Two weeks later on August 26, 2011, he announced via [[Twitter]] that instead he intended to reclassify again and attend the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|University of Connecticut]].{{cite news|first=Dom|last=Amore|title=Drummond Heading to UConn|url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-xpm-2011-08-26-hc-andre-drummond-uconn-20110826-story.html|newspaper=[[The Hartford Courant]]|date=August 26, 2011|access-date=March 26, 2019}} According to [[ESPN]], the decision "created a media frenzy due to the sheer surprise." Drummond had also been considering attending [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], or [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]].{{cite news |title=Writer roundtable: Three big questions |date=August 29, 2011 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/6905615 |access-date=September 1, 2011}}{{cite news|first=Dom|last=Amore|title= UConn Talks With Michael Bradley About Giving Up Scholarship|url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-xpm-2011-08-29-hc-uconn-mens-basketball-0830-20110829-story.html|newspaper=[[The Hartford Courant]]|date=August 29, 2011|access-date=March 26, 2019}}{{cite news|first=Dom|last=Amore|title=Drummond Officially On UConn Roster; Bradley Gives Up Scholarship|url=https://www.courant.com/news/connecticut/hc-xpm-2011-09-01-hc-uconn-men-drummond-bradley-0903-20110901-story.html|newspaper=[[The Hartford Courant]]|date=September 1, 2011|access-date=March 26, 2019}} Drummond appeared in 34 games as a freshman at UConn, starting 30 times.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/6585/type/mens-college-basketball |title=Andre Drummond Game By Game Stats and Performance – Connecticut (2011-12) |publisher=ESPN |access-date=August 1, 2026}} He averaged 28.4 minutes of playing time per game, during which he scored 10.0 points and grabbed 7.6 rebounds. He led the team in rebounds per game, blocks per game (2.7) and field goal percentage (.538). He scored 20-plus points in two games during the season, including a 24-point performance against [[Holy Cross Crusaders men's basketball|Holy Cross]], in which he shot 11-of-12 from the field. Drummond's collegiate career ended in the first round of the [[2012 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], as the ninth-seeded Huskies fell to eighth-seeded [[2011–12 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|Iowa State]]. The freshman center scored two points before fouling out in 26 minutes. A month later, Drummond announced his decision to enter the [[2012 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2012/story/_/id/7806984 |title=Andre Drummond to go pro |publisher=ESPN |date=April 13, 2012 |access-date=August 1, 2026|agency=Associated Press}} ==Professional career== ===Detroit Pistons (2012–2020)=== ====2012–15: Rookie season and first double-double seasons==== [[File:Andre Drummond and Anderson Varejao.jpg|thumb|left|Drummond defending [[Anderson Varejão]] in October 2013]] Drummond was selected by the [[Detroit Pistons]] with the ninth overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=David|last=Mayo|title=NBA Draft 2012: Detroit Pistons select Andre Drummond with No. 9 overall pick|url=http://www.mlive.com/pistons/index.ssf/2012/06/nba_draft_2012_detroit_pistons_1.html|work=MLive|date=June 29, 2012|access-date=March 23, 2019}} In his rookie season, Drummond averaged 7.9 points, 7.6 rebounds, 1.0 steal and 1.6 blocks in 20.7 minutes per game. On May 14, 2013, he was named to the [[2012–13 NBA season|2012–13]] [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/05/14/all-rookie-team-official-release/index.html |date=May 14, 2013 |title=Lillard headlines 2012–13 All-Rookie Team |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=July 19, 2013 fourth in NBA Rookie of the Year voting.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/05/01/kia-rookie-of-the-year-lillard/index.html |title=Portland's Lillard named 2012–13 Kia NBA Rookie of the Year |publisher=NBA |date=May 1, 2013 |access-date=May 1, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130504070715/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/05/01/kia-rookie-of-the-year-lillard/index.html |archive-date=May 4, 2013 |url-status=dead}} On January 24, 2014, Drummond recorded a then-career-high 20 rebounds to go with 20 points in a loss to the [[2013–14 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140124/NOPDET/gameinfo.html |title=Pelicans beat Pistons 103–101 on Gordon's layup |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |first=Noah |last=Trister |date=January 25, 2014 |access-date=January 25, 2014}} On February 14, Drummond scored 30 points and an [[NBA Rising Stars Challenge]] record 25 rebounds, and was named Sports Interactive, Inc. |date=February 14, 2014 |access-date=February 14, 2014}} On March 3, Drummond recorded 17 points and a then-career-high 26 rebounds in a win over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140303/NYKDET/gameinfo.html |title=Struggling Pistons beat slumping Knicks 96–85 |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |first=Larry |last=Lage |date=March 4, 2014 |access-date=March 4, 2014}} On March 11, 2015, Drummond recorded 22 points and a season-high 25 rebounds in a loss to the [[2014–15 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150311/DETGSW/gameinfo.html |title=Thompson, Warriors hold off Pistons for fifth straight win |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |first=Janie |last=McCauley |date=March 11, 2015 |access-date=March 20, 2015}} This was Drummond's fourth 20-point, 20-rebound game over the previous two seasons, the most in the NBA in that time span.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/features/drummond-dominates-glass-warriors-pull-away-spoil-spirited-pistons-effort |title=Drummond dominates glass, but Warriors pull away to spoil spirited Pistons effort |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |first=Keith |last=Langlois |date=March 12, 2015 |access-date=March 12, 2015}}{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400579252 |title=Warriors top Pistons for win No. 51, matching last season's total |publisher=ESPN |date=March 12, 2015 |access-date=March 12, 2015}} On March 29, Drummond recorded a then-career-high 32 points in a loss to the [[2014–15 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/features/too-much-wade-pistons-see-4-game-win-streak-snapped-playoff-shot-dwindle |title=Too much Wade as Pistons see 4-game win streak snapped, playoff shot dwindle |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |first=Keith |last=Langlois |date=March 29, 2015 |access-date=March 29, 2015}} ====2015–17: First All-Star selection and rebounding title==== Drummond recorded [[Double (basketball)#Double-double|double-doubles]] in each of the Pistons' first three games of the [[2015–16 NBA season|2015–16 season]], helping lead the team to an NBA-tying-best 3–0 record for the first time since the [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09 season]]. He became the first Pistons player to record three consecutive double-doubles to start the season since [[Ben Wallace (basketball)|Ben Wallace]] in [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151030/CHIDET/gameinfo.html |title=Pistons improve to 3–0, outlast Bulls 98–94 in OT |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |first=Noah |last=Trister |date=October 30, 2015 |access-date=October 30, 2015}} He was subsequently named the Eastern Conference [[2015–16 NBA season#Players of the week|Player of the Week]] for the first week of the season, becoming the first Piston to win the award since [[Rodney Stuckey]] did so in December 2009.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/andre-drummond-named-eastern-conference-player-week |title=Andre Drummond Named Eastern Conference Player of the Week |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |date=November 2, 2015 |access-date=November 2, 2015}} On November 3, Drummond recorded 25 points and a career-high 29 rebounds in a loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]], becoming the first Piston with back-to-back 20/20 games since 1985.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151103/INDDET/gameinfo.html |title=Pacers get first win, hand Pistons first loss this season |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |date=November 3, 2015 |access-date=November 3, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151104025445/http://www.nba.com/games/20151103/INDDET/gameinfo.html |archive-date=November 4, 2015 |url-status=dead}}{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/features/drummonds-dominance-cant-carry-pistons-4-0-start-bench-sputters-loss-pacers |title=Drummond's dominance can't carry Pistons to 4–0 start as bench sputters in loss to Pacers |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |first=Keith |last=Langlois |date=November 3, 2015 |access-date=November 3, 2015}} On November 8, he recorded 29 points and 27 rebounds in a win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], joining [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] and [[Wilt Chamberlain]] as the only players with three 20/20 games in the first six games of a season.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151108/DETPOR/gameinfo.html |title=Drummond leads Pistons to comeback 120–103 win over Blazers |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |first=Anne |last=Peterson |date=November 8, 2015 |access-date=November 8, 2015}} He was subsequently named the Eastern Conference Player of the Week for the second week of the season, becoming the first Piston to win player of the week in consecutive weeks, and the first player to win the award in the first two weeks of the season since [[LeBron James]] in [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/andre-drummond-named-eastern-conference-player-week-0 |title=Andre Drummond Named Eastern Conference Player of the Week |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |date=November 9, 2015 |access-date=November 9, 2015}} On November 21, Drummond's streak of 11 consecutive double-doubles to begin the season came to an end. This was the longest streak by a Piston since [[Dave DeBusschere]] recorded 13 consecutive double-doubles in [[1966–67 NBA season|1966–67]].{{cite web |url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2015/11/21/drummonds-double-double-streak-ends-pistons-loss/76200798/ |title=Drummond's double-double streak ends in Pistons' loss |newspaper=[[The Detroit News]] |first=Terry |last=Foster |date=November 21, 2015 |access-date=November 21, 2015}} On December 18, Drummond recorded 21 rebounds and a career-high 33 points in a 147–144 quadruple-overtime win over the [[Chicago Bulls]]. He became the first Pistons player with at least 30 points and 20 rebounds in a game since [[Dennis Rodman]] in [[1990–91 NBA season|1990–91]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/features/instant-classic-pistons-grind-out-4ot-win-chicago-amazing-night |title=Instant classic: Pistons grind out a 4OT win in Chicago on an amazing night |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |first=Keith |last=Langlois |date=December 18, 2015 |access-date=December 18, 2015}}{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151218/DETCHI/gameinfo.html |title=Drummond leads way, Pistons beat Bulls 147–144 in 4 OT |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |first=Andrew |last=Seligman |date=December 18, 2015 |access-date=December 19, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151220053332/http://www.nba.com/games/20151218/DETCHI/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 20, 2015 |url-status=dead}}{{cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2600643-pistons-vs-bulls-score-reaction-and-highlights-for-4ot-game |title=Pistons vs. Bulls: Score, Reaction and Highlights for 4OT Game |work=[[Bleacher Report]] |first=Danny |last=Webster |date=December 18, 2015 |access-date=December 18, 2015}} On January 20, 2016, Drummond set an NBA record for free throws missed in a game with 23, surpassing the previous record of 22 set by Wilt Chamberlain on December 1, 1967. He also set a career high and franchise record by attempting 36 free throws.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/features/pistons-open-2nd-half-big-road-win-houston-foil-hack-dre-excess |title=Pistons open 2nd half with big road win at Houston to foil Hack-a-Dre excess |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |first=Keith |last=Langlois |date=January 20, 2016 |access-date=January 20, 2016}}{{cite web |url=http://www.mlive.com/pistons/index.ssf/2016/01/pistons-rockets-running-gamer-.html |title=Andre Drummond sets NBA record for free throws missed; Pistons still win |publisher=MLive |first=David |last=Mayo |date=January 20, 2016 |access-date=January 20, 2016}} On January 28, Drummond earned his first [[NBA All-Star Game]] selection as a reserve for the Eastern Conference in the [[2016 NBA All-Star Game]].{{cite web |url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2016/01/28/only-idiots-would-say-drummond-isnt-all-star/79477524/ |title=Pistons' Drummond makes first All-Star Game |newspaper=[[The Detroit News]] |first=James |last=Hawkins |date=January 28, 2016 |access-date=January 28, 2016}} During the All-Star weekend, he also participated in the [[Slam Dunk Contest]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/andre-drummond-compete-2016-verizon-slam-dunk-contest-nba-all-star-weekend |title=Andre Drummond to Compete in 2016 Verizon Slam Dunk Contest at NBA All-Star Weekend |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |date=February 4, 2016 |access-date=February 4, 2016}} On February 27, he |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160227/DETMIL/gameinfo.html |title=3-point shooting helps lift Pistons to 102–91 win over Bucks |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |date=February 27, 2016 |access-date=February 27, 2016}}{{cite web | url = http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pistons-andre-drummond-league-leading-50th-double-double-saturday/ | title = Pistons' Andre Drummond: League-leading 50th double-double Saturday | publisher = [[CBS Interactive]] | work = [[CBS Sports]] | date = February 28, 2016 | access-date = February 28, 2016}} On March 2, Drummond recorded nine points and 14 rebounds against the San Antonio Spurs, ending his career high and the league's season high of consecutive double-doubles at 13 straight.{{cite web | url = build on sweep by Cavaliers|url=https://www.theoaklandpress.com/sports/pistons-hoping-to-build-on-sweep-by-cavaliers/article_3269b883-7012-5e09-866c-dc5fe36dcde2.html|website=The Oakland [[File:Andre Drummond (31577442391).jpg|upright=0.85|thumb|Drummond with the Pistons in 2016]] On July 15, 2016, Drummond re-signed with the Pistons on a five-year, $130 million contract.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-re-sign-center-andre-drummond |title=Detroit Pistons Re-Sign Center Andre Drummond |work=NBA.com |date=July 15, 2016 |access-date=July 15, 2016}}{{cite web |last=Stein |first=Marc |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/16675680 |title=Andre Drummond, Pistons agree on five-year max deal |work=ESPN.com |date=July 1, 2016 |access-date=July 15, 2016}} On October 30, he recorded 20 points and 23 rebounds in a 98–83 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], setting his 10th career game with at least 20 points and 20 rebounds.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899488 |title=Drummond's big night leads Pistons over Bucks 98–83 |work=ESPN.com |date=October 30, 2016 |access-date=October 30, 2016}} With 20 points and 17 rebounds on November 19 against the [[Boston Celtics]], Drummond reached 4,000 career rebounds. At 23 years and 101 days, he became the second-youngest player to reach the milestone, trailing only [[Dwight Howard]] (22 years, 129 days).{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899638 |title=Celtics win in Detroit on Horford's follow in final seconds |work=ESPN.com |date=November 19, 2016 |access-date=November 20, 2016}} On December 7, he recorded a season-high 26 points and 20 rebounds in an 87–77 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899763 |title=Walker's big 4th quarter lifts Hornets past Pistons 87–77 |work=ESPN.com |date=December 7, 2016 |access-date=December 8, 2016}} On March 17, 2017, he grabbed 22 rebounds in an 87–75 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]]. It was the 34th time he had 20 rebounds in a game, including seven in 2016–17.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900418|title=Big fourth quarter lifts Raptors past Pistons 87–75|work=ESPN.com|date=March 17, 2017|access-date=March 18, 2017}} ====2017–20: Second All-Star selection and consecutive rebounding titles==== On October 23, 2017, Drummond recorded 14 points and 14 rebounds in a 97–86 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He moved into sixth place on Detroit's career rebounding list, passing [[Walter Dukes]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974792|title=Ben Simmons has triple-double in fourth game, Joel Embiid adds 30 in 76ers' win|work=ESPN.com|date=October 23, 2017|access-date=October 23, 2017}} Two days later, in a 122–101 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], Drummond recorded his 5,000th career rebound in the first quarter, becoming the sixth Pistons player to reach that total. At 24 years, 76 days, he became the second-youngest player to reach the milestone, trailing only [[Dwight Howard]] (23 years, 112 days).{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974807|title=Harris scores 34, Pistons rout Timberwolves 122–101|work=ESPN.com|date=October 25, 2017|access-date=October 25, 2017}}{{cite web|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2017/10/25/pistons-center-andre-drummond-dwight-howard-wilt-chamberlain/801375001/|title=Pistons' Andre Drummond off to Dwight Howard-Wilt Chamberlain start|newspaper=Detroit Free Press|first=Chris|last=Nielsen|date=October 25, 2017|access-date=October 25, 2017}} On November 10, he recorded 16 points, 20 rebounds and a then-career-high seven assists in a 111–104 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]], moving the Pistons to a 9–3 record—their best start to a season since the 2005–06 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974920|title=Drummond, Jackson lead Pistons past Atlanta 111–104|work=ESPN.com|date=November 10, 2017|access-date=November 10, 2017}} Drummond went on to become the first player to grab at least 200 rebounds in the first 13 games of two different seasons since [[Dennis Rodman]] did it three times for three different teams in the 1990s.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974968|title=Stephenson rallies Pacers from 22 down past Pistons 107–100|work=ESPN.com|date=November 17, 2017|access-date=November 17, 2017}} On November 27, he recorded season highs of 26 points and 22 rebounds in a 118–108 win over the [[Boston Celtics]]. He also had six assists and four steals, becoming the first player with that many points, rebounds, assists and steals since [[Charles Barkley]] in January 1990.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975043|title=Drummond (26 pts, 22 reb) leads Pistons past Celtics 118–108|work=ESPN.com|date=November 27, 2017|access-date=November 27, 2017}} On December 14, Drummond recorded 12 points, 19 rebounds and a career-high eight assists in a 105–91 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975164|title=Drummond helps Pistons beat Hawks to snap 7-game skid|work=ESPN.com|date=December 14, 2017|access-date=December 14, 2017}} On January 24, Drummond recorded 30 points, 24 rebounds, six blocked shots, four assists and three steals in a 98–95 overtime loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/pistons/index.ssf/2018/01/pistons_andre_drummond_on_hist.html|title=Pistons' Andre Drummond on historic night: 'It just wasn't enough'|work=MLive.com|first=Ansar|last=Khan|date=January 24, 2018|access-date=January 24, 2018}} He became the first player to record such stats in a game since 1973–74, when the NBA first began to record blocks and steals. During the game, Drummond reached 2,000 offensive rebounds for his career, becoming the youngest player to reach the milestone at 24 years, 167 days, surpassing the previous record held by Howard at 25 years, 86 days.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975448|title=Jazz rally late in 4th, beat Pistons 98–95 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=January 24, 2018|access-date=January 24, 2018}} On January 30, he was named as a replacement for [[John Wall]] in the [[2018 NBA All-Star Game]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22268114 |title=Pistons' Andre Drummond replaces injured John Wall of Wizards for All-Star Game|work=ESPN.com|date=January 30, 2018|access-date=January 30, 2018}} On February 3, he recorded 23 points, 20 rebounds, four steals and four blocks in a 111–107 win over the [[Miami Heat]]. Drummond had at least 20 points and 20 rebounds for the sixth time in 2017–18 and became the first player with at least 20 points, 20 rebounds, four steals and four blocks since [[Hakeem Olajuwon]] on December 22, 1989.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975522|title=Pistons win again with Griffin, 111–107 over Heat|work=ESPN.com|date=February 3, 2018|access-date=February 4, 2018}} Four days later, he recorded 17 points and a season-high 27 rebounds in a 115–106 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975551|title=Drummond, Griffin leads Pistons over Nets 115–106|work=ESPN.com|date=February 7, 2018|access-date=February 7, 2018}} On March 29, he recorded 24 points and 23 rebounds in a 103–92 win over the [[Washington Wizards]]. It was his 20th 20/20 game of his career, the most of any NBA player since he joined the league in 2012.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975870|title=Drummond's 20–20 game leads Pistons past Wizards|work=ESPN.com|date=March 29, 2018|access-date=March 29, 2018}} Drummond concluded the regular season averaging 16 rebounds per game, becoming the first player since Rodman in 1997 to average 16 rebounds per game in a season and only the second player in the last 40 years.{{cite web|last=Mickle|first=Shane|url=https://clutchpoints.com/pistons-news-andre-drummond-second-player-40-years-average-16-rebounds/|title=Andre Drummond second player in 40 years to average more than 16 rebounds|work=clutchpoints.com|date=April 11, 2018|access-date=April 11, 2018}} On November 5, 2018, Drummond recorded 25 points and 24 rebounds in a 120–115 overtime loss to the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070821|title=Richardson scores 27, leads Heat past Pistons 120–115 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=November 5, 2018|access-date=January 17, 2019}} On January 31, Drummond recorded 24 points and 20 rebounds in a 93–89 victory over the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. During the game, he became the Pistons' all-time career leader in offensive rebounds with 2,431, surpassing the previous record held by [[Bill Laimbeer]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071437|title=Pistons edge short-handed Mavericks 93–89|work=ESPN.com|date=January 31, 2019|access-date=January 31, 2019}} On February 8, he had his ninth 20/20 game of the season with 29 points and 20 rebounds in a 120–103 win over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071490|title=Pistons hand Knicks 15th straight loss, 120–103|work=ESPN.com|date=February 8, 2019|access-date=February 8, 2019}} On February 11, Drummond scored a season-high 32 points against the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/drumman01/gamelog/2019/|title=Andre Drummond 2018–19 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=May 23, 2019}} On March 8, he recorded 20 points and 24 rebounds, including 14 points and 18 rebounds in the second half, to help the Pistons overcome a 21-point deficit in a 112–104 victory over the [[Chicago Bulls]]. This was Drummond's league-leading 11th 20/20 game of the season. He was subsequently named the [[2018–19 NBA season#Players of the Week|Eastern Conference Player of the Week]]. He averaged 22.3 points (67% FG), 18.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.3 blocks and 1.3 steals per game in three games.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/andre-drummond-named-eastern-conference-player-week-190311 |title=Andre Drummond Named Eastern Conference Player of the Week |work=NBA.com |date=March 11, 2019|access-date=March 11, 2019}} On March 11 against the [[Brooklyn Nets]], Drummond's 19th straight double-double tied him with [[Bob Lanier]] (1974–75) for the longest such streak in Pistons' team history.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071676|title=Nets rout Pistons 103–75 to move into No. 6 spot in East|work=ESPN.com|date=March 11, 2019|access-date=March 12, 2019}} His was a member of the [[2014 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team|2014 U.S. national team]] that won the gold medal at the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup]]. Over the span of the tournament, he averaged 3.0 points and 2.5 rebounds in eight games.{{cite web |title=Andre DRUMMOND at the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2014 |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/player/Andre-Drummond |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=January 7, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200107123130/http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/player/Andre-Drummond |archive-date=January 7, 2020}} ==Personal life== Drummond has three children, two daughters and a son.{{cite web |agency=Associated Press| title=Drummond's daughter steals the show in presser after Brooklyn Nets win | website=MARCA | date=2022-03-27 | url=https://www.marca.com/en/basketball/nba/brooklyn-nets/2022/03/27/624046a6268e3efa728b45cb.html | access-date=2025-12-13}} Drummond briefly dated American writer and former actress [[Jennette McCurdy]] during his rookie year.{{cite web |title= Jennette McCurdy and Andre Drummond's brief fling in 2013 sends fans wild |url=https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2022/06/23/jennette-mccurdy-andre-drummond/ |website=hitc.com|date=June 23, 2022 |url-status=dead}} He has been an Ambassador for [[Special Olympics]] since 2016.{{cite web |title=Andre Drummond Global Ambassador |url=https://www.specialolympics.org/about/ambassadors/andre-drummond |website=specialolympics.org}} Andre has started and funded a music development program for person with disabilities in conjunction with the [[Berklee College of Music]] of Massachusetts. The initial phase of the program began in 2025 in Middletown, Connecticut. The program, known as "Team Andre" trains persons to give the required specialized instruction to persons with physical and mental disabilities to teach them to play a variety of instruments and later to become involved with musical groups of sorts.{{Cite web |title=Community Health Musician Certificate
